name: Sahih al-Bukhari
author: Imam Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Bukhari
introduction: Sahih al-Bukhari is the most authentic book after the Qur'an, compiled by Imam al-Bukhari (810-870 CE). It contains 7,563 hadiths (including repetitions) across 97 books covering every aspect of life.

name: Sahih Muslim
author: Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj al-Naysaburi
introduction: Sahih Muslim is the second most authentic hadith collection, compiled by Imam Muslim (817-875 CE). It contains 7,470 hadiths across 56 books, complementing Sahih al-Bukhari.

name: Sunan Abi Dawud
author: Imam Abu Dawud al-Sijistani
introduction: Sunan Abi Dawud is one of the six major hadith collections, compiled by Imam Abu Dawud (817-889 CE). It focuses primarily on legal hadiths (ahkam) and contains 5,274 hadiths.

name: Jami' al-Tirmidhi
author: Imam Muhammad ibn Isa al-Tirmidhi
introduction: Jami' al-Tirmidhi is one of the six major hadith collections, compiled by Imam al-Tirmidhi (824-892 CE). It is distinguished by its grading of hadiths and discussion of legal opinions.

name: Sunan al-Nasa'i
author: Imam Ahmad ibn Shu'ayb al-Nasa'i
introduction: Sunan al-Nasa'i is one of the six major hadith collections, compiled by Imam al-Nasa'i (829-915 CE). It is considered the most authentic of the four Sunan after the two Sahihs.

name: Sunan Ibn Majah
author: Imam Ibn Majah al-Qazwini
introduction: Sunan Ibn Majah is the sixth of the major hadith collections, compiled by Imam Ibn Majah (824-887 CE). It contains 4,341 hadiths across 37 books.
